answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before it may trade. Creating a hundred fake identities then costs a hundred stakes, while honest agents recover theirs. A harbor registry issues one credential per verified stake, and peers check it before attesting work. A Sybil that behaves badly loses its pearl of reputation, its stake is slashed, and its credential is revoked, so the attack cost scales linearly with fake identities while honest participation stays cheap.
